mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals strengthening economic demand, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending power increases.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% month-over-month signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic output slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% month-over-month signals a strengthening demand for housing, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing sector contributes positively to GDP.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a rising unemployment rate and a decrease in nonfarm payrolls signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending decrease.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect between UNRATE and PAYEMS on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index by more than 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and the Fed may tighten policy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a high level of real personal consumption expenditures signals strong consumer demand, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending drives corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS levels and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
